basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: Identifies a published edition, distinct from the abstract work and from any single copy or file.
An ISBN, ISSN or DOI identifies a specific target and must not be reused for other editions or formats.
A publication date or catalogue record is not proof of lawful publication or authorship.
Corrections and retractions are recorded as new states, not by changing the published text.

mustNot: Assign identifiers on behalf of a registration agency.

considerations: Correct attribution matters to authors' rights and careers.
Retractions must stay visible so readers are not misled.
Accessible editions serve readers with disabilities.

items: An edition has a title, edition statement, publisher, publication date and identifiers.
Often confused with the work, a manifestation file and a physical copy.
